name: Joshua
overview: Joshua was a male figure who served as the high priest during the time of the prophet Haggai, as noted in Haggai 1:1. While his tribal affiliation is not specified, his priestly role places him at the center of Israel's religious leadership in the post-exilic period. There are no additional notes recorded about his background.
namesAndTitles: The name Joshua means 'YHWH saves,' highlighting God's saving power. Additionally, he is called 'Branch,' a title given by God, which symbolizes growth and restoration, as referenced in Zechariah 3:8. These names together emphasize God's role in salvation and the hope of renewal through Joshua.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Joshua as the son of Jehozadak in Haggai 1:1. Beyond this paternal relationship, there are no other family connections recorded for him.
scriptureSignificance: Joshua's significance lies in his leadership as high priest during a critical period of Israel's restoration after exile. His role connects to the broader biblical theme of God's salvation and covenant faithfulness, prefigured by his name and the divine title 'Branch.' Through him, God’s people were spiritually renewed and reminded of their calling to serve the Lord faithfully.

keyEvents.event: Led Israel in battle against Amalek
